speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Yet, we must not mistake political dominance for political stability.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Single party dominance brought us here, but we cannot assume it will guarantee stability ahead.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Even the People's Action Party (PAP) acknowledges a growing appetite for more voices in Parliament, more diversity in policy-making.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is why the Workers' Party (WP) continues to push for the further strengthening of our parliamentary institutions, whether through electoral reforms or select committee work, as previously called for by Aljunied Member of Parliament (MP) Gerald Giam.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Parliament is sovereign and the bedrock on which our Government derives is legitimacy.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: We should not view increases in legislative work, including Select Committee work as a drain on time and resources.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Parliament's duty and responsibility to the public is to continuously strive for rigorous oversight and active legislative work.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: To strengthen our parliamentary democracy, we must ensure that we have safeguards and institutions to define our politics, particularly, the delineation and interaction between partisan and non-partisan roles.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And as we move forward towards a more diverse and representative political and parliamentary landscape, it is reasonable to properly delineate what is and what is not partisan.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is especially important when we turn our attention to who sits in this House.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Otherwise, how do we stop ourselves from wondering whether a Member is auditioning for another role or a different office each time they rise to speak?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I would not be breaking any rules if I retired from electoral politics, quit the WP, left my seat, declared myself non-partisan and applied to be an Nominated Member of Parliament (NMP) the next day.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If I did this, Singaporeans would and should ask whether this passes the smell test, wonder about our parliamentary institutions and whether it is enough to just keep to the letter of the law.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Distinctions between partisan and non-partisan roles should apply to those leaving political appointments, the presidency and senior public sector roles too.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Public servants seeking political office should observe a cooling-off period.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Political appointees and senior public servants leaving service office should not immediately be employed in areas they last oversaw or regulated to avoid actual or apparent conflicts of interest.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In Singapore, under our Code of Corporate Governance, independent directors must generally have a three-year gap from any prior executive role before being regarded as independent.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It appears that our civil service has similar restrictions and principles.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: In 2012, the Indian Election Commission muted a cooling-off period clause to prevent civil servants from joining electoral politics straight after they resign to give these persons time to dissociate from their previous roles and deter civil servants from acting or auditioning to gain favour for candidacy.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This idea was previously raised by Leon Pereira and I want to repeat this call.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: These restrictions are not about in the individual trustworthiness.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: They exist because systems must provide clear, defensible boundaries against conflicts of interest, perceived or real.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is about enhancing and concretising protections for the integrity of political institutions, especially at a time when lines may be easily blurred in the public eye.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The PAP's position is that grassroots advisers under the People's Association (PA) advances the policies of a sitting administration, or the PA does important work and may bring into and policies into our communities.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Is the role of the grassroots advisor a non-partisan public function or is it a partisan extension of the governing party's ground operations?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If the role is a non-partisan extension of the state, then individuals occupying those roles must be non-partisan, like the civil service.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: They do not carry partisan loyalties into their roles, nor do their appointments hinge on electoral fortunes.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Their credibility depends on discharging their duties without fear or favour, regardless of administration.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The present design of the grassroots advisors system attempts both: non-partisan in theory while requiring political alignment in practice.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It would be helpful to provide clarity on which side grassroots advisors fall on.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This also has implications on how grassroots activists see their role.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If grassroots activists are involved in electioneering, what are the lines between partisanship and non-partisanship?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The rules are apparent for civil servants but less so for grassroots activists and PA staff.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If the grassroots advisers structure is genuinely non-partisan and functions like part of the civil service ecosystem, would partisanship be appropriate?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, the gist of this cut was strengthening parliamentary democracy and safeguarding democracy in a changing world.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Watching recent events unfold on the global stage, it sometimes feels like democracy is under siege.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In some other countries, which have long been regarded as leading democracies, there is a sense that systems are breaking down, trust has been eroded and once-revered institutions have been rendered ineffective, compromised or even under direct attack.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This malaise is marked by the following symptoms: polarisation, deep divisions with no space for a middle ground, sometimes resulting in legislative paralysis; political contestation, increasingly framed around race, religion or other divisive issues which exploit and deepen divisions; populism, where electorates are sold only the upsides and not told the downsides, and where difficult but necessary decisions are avoided; short-term thinking driven by selfish political calculation without regard to societal cost; performative politics in and out of Parliament, in lieu of substantive and rational discourse; misleading statements or even not so rarely, outright falsehoods; disregard of the rule of law and processes.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We can be thankful that our Parliamentary democracy is not in such a parlous state.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is not because we are immune to such dangers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are as vulnerable to these political pitfalls as any other society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have, in large part, avoided going down this path only because we and, in particular, successive PAP Governments have continued to maintain high standards and important fundamentals.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this is not to say it cannot happen to us in the future.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And it takes very little to get onto the slippery slope.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: How then can we safeguard our Parliamentary democracy?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One must observe the letter and the spirit of the rules and to follow through, even though the consequences may be politically inconvenient.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Around the world, we see democracies with many laws but that are still dysfunctional.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need Parliamentarians with competence, commitment and conscience on both sides of the House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In Government, we need competent people who understand the fundamentals of governance and can master the difficult task of running a country.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In opposition, we need competent people who understand the issues, ask the right questions and hold not only the Government, but also themselves to the same high standards of integrity and accountability.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We need Parliamentarians who are committed, who will stay the course and are able to put country before party.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One was on cooling-off periods and the other on grassroots advisors.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On the question of cooling-off periods, actually, it is very straightforward or simple.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I think she put forward the suggestion or the scenario – could she resign from the WP and become a Nominated Member of Parliament (NMP) the following day?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You have declared to the world that you are no longer partisan.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You have taken on a responsibility to be non-partisan and so long as you carry out that duty properly, there is nothing wrong with that.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And should the reverse be the same or take place, meaning that you are in a non-partisan position and let us say, tomorrow you wish to become partisan, then the right thing to do would be to step down from your non-partisan position and say to the world that you intend to have a partisan role or are exploring a partisan role.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That way, it is transparent, it is fair and this is what we have done in our system, and it has served us well.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She mentioned conflicts of interest, perceived or real.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Because a conflict of interest can also arise where you may have taken a certain position in Parliament and then later, be sitting on a tribunal which has to decide on an issue where you have already taken a position in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Now, that would be a conflict of interest too.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, we must see how we conduct ourselves appropriately and much depends on the individual.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is one of the reasons why Members of Parliament (MPs) should, in the gist when they file their cuts, actually set out a bit more on what they are going to say.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, first, it is wrongly filed under this cut.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, I do not propose to address it in detail, other than to say that this has been answered quite fully by Minister Ong Ye Kung in a separate earlier session of Parliament, where he explained the difference between the role of a grassroots advisor, which is essentially flowing from Government, and that of an MP.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The MP's role is to come to Parliament to represent their voters and to do certain things and the roles are separate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, let me just wrap up by pointing to a speech made by Deputy Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong in 1988 about the infamous Hendrickson affair.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He cited three political models: one, the American system of checks and balances, where the underlying premises is fundamentally one of distrust, where each branch must constantly keep the other in check; the other, the British system, where the executive, the Prime Minister and Cabinet are given wider discretionary powers.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, Ms He, it has to be a very short clarification.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In total, we only have one and a half minutes, so that is for you and the Minister to respond.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: So, is the Minister saying that if directors or formerly executive officers in a company actually step down and declare that they are henceforth independent, that that would suffice?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I do not want to pre-empt nor speak for the panel at this stage.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: But also just to clarify that the Motion that was tabled before Parliament was on many limbs.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: None of them were about contravening the party's constitution, which is what we were tasked to look into, and when it came to actually voting about the Motion, I felt that because of the many limbs in there, I felt that was something that I could not support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What is of importance is what is the right and appropriate conduct for MPs, and I have outlined that earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the second point about conflicts of interest, the resolution that was discussed did touch on matters which will be something that the Central Executive Committee or the disciplinary tribunal of the WP has to look at.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I say no more than that because it is self-evident and self-explanatory.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms He, I would like to invite you to withdraw your amendment.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: And with that I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
